title: eval-harness: add per-prompt regression CI hooks and quality gating enhancements
author: Aisha Patel
description: This PR adds per-prompt regression hooks to the eval-harness CI pipeline and enhances quality gating so teams can detect prompt-set regressions at merge-time. Motivation: As we onboard more prompt-sets and per-customer evaluation criteria, a single aggregate regression signal is noisy and causes both false positives and hidden regressions. This change implements: 1) per-prompt CI hooks that run a focused eval subset for changed prompts or mapped prompt keys; 2) configurable per-prompt quality thresholds (accuracy/score/delta) with sensible defaults and a strict-median fallback; 3) integration with the existing eval-metrics reporter so PR checks post per-prompt metrics to GitHub checks and Linear; 4) a small CLI helper (redwood-eval ci-hook) to locally run the same gating logic; 5) lightweight caching of prompt results to reduce CI time for large prompt-sets. The description below lists the key user-facing changes and the internal implementation notes. Checklist: [x] unit + integration tests added for gating logic, [x] CI job definition updated, [x] docs updated (docs/eval-harness/ci-gates.md), [x] Linear ENG-4123 linked, [x] performance validated (median CI runtime increase ~12% for full-suite, incremental gating typically <30s). Backwards compatibility: old aggregate gating remains as an opt-in mode (env REDWOOD_EVAL_AGGREGATE=true). Rollout: feature enabled by default for repos using per-prompt manifests; can be disabled by repo-level config. See release_notes for quick summary.

release_notes: Add per-prompt regression CI hooks and quality gating: enables focused prompt-set regression detection, configurable per-prompt thresholds with median fallback, CLI helper for local testing, and GitHub CI integration. Minor runtime overhead; opt-out supported via repo config.
summary: Adds per-prompt evaluation gating to the eval-harness CI, improves signal-to-noise for prompt regressions, and wires metrics to GitHub checks and Linear for visibility. Includes tests, docs, and a local CLI helper.
